name: Oxford Blue
lede: Oxford blue is a very dark blue named for the University of Oxford, whose sporting color it is.

sections.title: A university's blue
sections.body:
Paterson defines Oxford blue as a dark blue [1]. The entry for *blue* explains why: a person who represents Oxford or Cambridge in a sport is called a blue, wearing dark blue for Oxford and light blue for Cambridge [2]. The honor itself is also called a blue [2].

The light partner is [[cambridge-blue]]; other dark blues nearby include [[royal-blue]] and navy. Paterson also lists Oxford grey, a dark grey, and Oxford chrome, a yellow ochre, so the university lent its name to more than one color [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of museum paintings, a color near this swatch is present in 27 works, 0.11 per cent of the archive [3]. The earliest is a work of about 1400 in the National Gallery of Art, and the latest dates from 1923 [3]. As photographed, a very dark blue like this one is hard to tell from black, so these counts are approximate [3].
